modules.title: 登录状态怎样随请求往返

items.title: 响应先提出保存要求
items.text: 服务器在响应中发送 `Set-Cookie`，浏览器根据 Cookie 的名称、作用域和安全属性决定是否保存。

items.title: 后续请求按条件自动携带
items.text: 访问匹配的地址时，浏览器会把可发送的 Cookie 放进 `Cookie` 请求头。HttpOnly Cookie 不能被页面脚本读取，但仍可随请求发送。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: Cookie 与 localStorage 都能把数据留在浏览器，但 Cookie 会按规则进入 HTTP 请求。Cookie 本身不是完整认证系统，也不是数据库；服务器仍需验证会话、身份和每项操作的权限。敏感会话应在 HTTPS 下结合 Secure、HttpOnly，并按跨站需求选择 SameSite。

lessonPractice.title: 登录接口返回成功，但刷新后用户又变成未登录。下一步最应该检查什么？

options.label: 检查响应是否设置会话 Cookie，以及刷新后的请求是否带回它
options.feedback: 对。要沿着设置、保存、携带这三步检查，才能判断服务器为何无法在下一次请求识别会话。

options.label: 在 localStorage 里写入 isLoggedIn=true，让页面继续显示登录态
options.feedback: 前端标记只能改变页面显示，不能证明服务器认可会话，也不能代替请求中携带的凭证。

options.label: 只检查数据库里的用户记录，不查看浏览器和请求头
options.feedback: 用户记录存在不代表这次浏览器请求带有可识别的会话；还要查看 Set-Cookie 和后续 Cookie 头。

en.title: The login API returns success, but a refresh makes the user signed out again. What should you inspect first?

options.label: Check whether the response sets a session cookie and the refresh request sends it back
options.feedback: Correct. Follow the set, store, and send steps to learn why the server cannot recognize the session on the next request.

options.label: Write isLoggedIn=true to localStorage so the page keeps showing a signed-in state
options.feedback: A frontend flag changes display only. It does not prove that the server accepts a session or replace a request credential.

options.label: Inspect only the user record in the database, not the browser or request headers
options.feedback: An existing user record does not mean this browser request carries a recognizable session. Check Set-Cookie and the later Cookie header too.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请检查登录响应是否设置了安全的会话 Cookie，以及刷新后的受保护请求是否自动携带它。不要打印完整 Cookie 值；用 Network 和 Storage 验证刷新后仍登录，并确认真正的身份与权限判断仍在后端完成。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Check whether the login response sets a secure session cookie and whether the protected request after refresh sends it automatically. Do not print the full cookie value; use Network and Storage to verify the session survives refresh, while identity and authorization remain server-side.

learning.assumes: You have seen a site stay signed in after a refresh and know that browsers can keep some site data.
learning.outcome: You can trace Set-Cookie, browser storage, and the later Cookie request header to inspect a session, and distinguish cookies from Web Storage and backend authentication.

modules.title: How a login state travels with requests
The three steps in a cookie round trip

items.title: The response asks the browser to store it
items.text: The server sends `Set-Cookie` in a response, and the browser decides whether to store it from its name, scope, and security attributes.

items.title: Later requests send it when conditions match
items.text: For a matching address, the browser puts sendable cookies in the `Cookie` request header. An HttpOnly cookie cannot be read by page script but can still be sent with a request.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: Cookies and localStorage can both keep data in a browser, but cookies enter HTTP requests by rule. A cookie is not a complete authentication system or a database; the server must still verify the session, identity, and permission for each action. Sensitive sessions should use Secure and HttpOnly over HTTPS and choose SameSite for the cross-site need.

distinctions.label: Browser storage
distinctions.text: {c:cookie} is automatically considered for matching HTTP requests; {c:browser-storage} is read by page code and is not automatically sent as a request header.

distinctions.label: Authentication
distinctions.text: {c:cookie} can carry a session identifier between browser and server; {c:authentication} is the server-side process of verifying who the requester is.
